I’ve been farming this wheat-maize rotation for six years now, and I know what works on my 40 mu in Quzhou. I don’t have book learning, but I watch my neighbors, listen to the seed shop, and learn from my own eyes. The double cropping here is tight—winter wheat goes in after National Day, comes out around early June, and then maize goes in right behind it before the summer heat peaks.

For wheat this year, I’ll plant an improved variety that resists lodging and does well with our well water. I’ll spread compound fertilizer as base and top-dress urea at green-up and jointing. I’ll irrigate three times: once before winter to help it establish, once at jointing, and once at grain filling when the spring drought hits. I’ll spray herbicide early and fungicide once if I see rust. I rotary-till before sowing to break up the stubble and level the field.

For maize, I’ll sow hybrid seed the same day or the day after wheat harvest—no time to waste. I usually do no-tillage for maize to save time and keep moisture, just clear the stubble and plant. I’ll apply fertilizer at sowing and side-dress nitrogen at the big flare stage. I’ll irrigate twice if the summer is hot and dry, especially at flowering. I’ll spray pesticide twice: once for weeds and once for corn borer if I spot moths.
